# Flow Config Editor Kit — complete reference for coding agents

Single-file reference for building a Salesforce Flow **custom property editor** with this framework. Everything needed is on this page; you should not have to open another file.

Unnamespaced package. Components resolve under the `c` namespace: `c/flowConfigEditorBase`, `c-flow-config-value-input`, and so on.

---

## 1. What this framework is for

A Flow **screen component** (an LWC exposed to `lightning__FlowScreen`) can declare a **custom property editor** — another LWC that renders the configuration panel a Flow admin sees in Flow Builder.

Flow Builder hands that editor four inputs and expects specific events back. This framework supplies both sides: a base class that owns the contract, and pickers that browse Flow resources, Salesforce objects, SObject fields, and Apex-defined types.

Two files are involved:

1. the **screen component** (`myComponent`) — declares its properties in `myComponent.js-meta.xml`
2. the **editor** (`myComponentEditor`) — extends `c/flowConfigEditorBase`

---

## 2. Wire the editor to the component

In the screen component's `.js-meta.xml`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<LightningComponentBundle xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
    <apiVersion>67.0</apiVersion>
    <isExposed>true</isExposed>
    <masterLabel>My Component</masterLabel>
    <targets>
        <target>lightning__FlowScreen</target>
    </targets>
    <targetConfigs>
        <targetConfig targets="lightning__FlowScreen" configurationEditor="c-my-component-editor">
            <!-- Declare the generic SObject type BEFORE any property that uses it. -->
            <propertyType name="T" extends="SObject" label="Record Type" />

            <property name="records" type="{T[]}" label="Records" role="inputOnly" />
            <property name="objectApiName" type="String" label="Object API Name" role="inputOnly" />
            <property name="displayField" type="String" label="Display Field" role="inputOnly" />
            <property name="heading" type="String" label="Heading" role="inputOnly" />
            <property name="pageSize" type="Integer" label="Page Size" role="inputOnly" />

            <!-- Optional: Flow supplies its runtime API version, which the
                 editor passes to pickers for versioned $Api globals. -->
            <property
                name="flowRuntimeApiVersion"
                type="Double"
                label="Flow Runtime API Version"
                role="inputOnly"
                flowRole="flowRuntimeApiVersion"
            />
        </targetConfig>
    </targetConfigs>
</LightningComponentBundle>
```

Rules that are easy to get wrong:

- `configurationEditor` uses the **kebab-case element name** (`c-my-component-editor`), not the camelCase module name.
- A generic SObject needs **both** a `<propertyType name="T" extends="SObject" label="..."/>` declaration and a property typed `{T}` (single) or `{T[]}` (collection). Declaring only the property will not deploy.
- `<propertyType>` elements must come before the `<property>` elements that reference them.
- The type letter is arbitrary but must match the `genericType` in your schema, or the `typeName` you pass to `setGenericType()`.
- Use a **distinct** type name per independent collection (`TSingle`, `TMultiple`). Sharing one across unrelated collections couples them.
- Every declared generic type **must** end up mapped, or the Flow cannot be activated.
- Property types are Salesforce metadata types: `String`, `Integer`, `Double`, `Boolean`, `Date`, `DateTime`, `{T}`, `{T[]}`. There is no `Number` and no `Field` type. A schema `type: "Number"` maps to an `Integer` or `Double` property.
- A field selection persists as a `String`; multiple fields persist as a JSON array inside a `String`.
- `role="inputOnly"` on every property the editor writes; omit it only for genuine output properties.
- The editor bundle needs `isExposed=false` and **no** `targets` or `targetConfigs`.

---

## 3. The editor — declarative form (default)

```js
import FlowConfigEditorBase from "c/flowConfigEditorBase";

export default class MyComponentEditor extends FlowConfigEditorBase {
  static flowProperties = {
    records: {
      type: "SObject",
      collection: true,
      genericType: "T",
      objectProperty: "objectApiName",
      required: true,
      label: "Records"
    },
    displayField: { type: "field", dependsOn: "records", required: true },
    heading: { type: "String" }
  };
}
```

That is the complete editor. **No `.html` file. No event handlers.** The base renders controls, hydrates saved values, keeps the generic mapping in step, clears dependent fields on object-type change, and implements `validate()`.

The editor's `.js-meta.xml`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<LightningComponentBundle xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
    <apiVersion>67.0</apiVersion>
    <isExposed>false</isExposed>
</LightningComponentBundle>
```

### Schema keys

| Key              | Applies to | Meaning                                                               |
| ---------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`           | all        | `String`, `Number`, `SObject`, `field`. Default `String`.             |
| `label`          | all        | Default is the humanized property name.                               |
| `required`       | all        | Reports `"<label> is required."`                                      |
| `helpText`       | all        | Help text beside the label.                                           |
| `placeholder`    | all        | Empty-state text.                                                     |
| `collection`     | `SObject`  | Restrict picker to collections.                                       |
| `genericType`    | `SObject`  | Generic type name kept in step with the selection.                    |
| `objectProperty` | `SObject`  | Optional String property mirroring the resolved object API name.      |
| `allowManual`    | `SObject`  | Allow a hand-typed reference. Default `true`.                         |
| `dependsOn`      | `field`    | Property supplying the object API name.                               |
| `multiple`       | `field`    | Ordered multi-field selection, persisted as JSON.                     |
| `sortable`       | `field`    | Show drag, position, and arrow controls in multiple mode. Selected rows and removal remain visible when false. Default `true`. |
| `allowCustom`    | `field`    | Enable the field/resource header switch. Default `false`.             |
| `customModeProperty` | `field` | Boolean Flow property used to persist the selected mode.              |
| `acceptedTypes`  | `field`    | Comma-separated field types.                                          |

Declaration order is render order.

---

## 4. The editor — imperative form (escape hatch)

Use when the schema cannot express something: conditional requiredness, legacy property migration, cross-property rules, custom layout. Same base class — mix freely with a schema.

```js
import FlowConfigEditorBase from "c/flowConfigEditorBase";

export default class MyComponentEditor extends FlowConfigEditorBase {
  get heading() {
    return this.input("heading");
  }

  get headingDataType() {
    return this.inputDataType("heading", "String");
  }

  handleHeadingChange(event) {
    this.clearErrors();
  }

  validateConfiguration() {
    return this.heading ? [] : [{ key: "heading", errorString: "Heading is required." }];
  }
}
```

With its own `myComponentEditor.html`:

```html
<template>
  <c-flow-config-value-input
    data-validatable
    data-property="heading"
    label="Heading"
    property-name="heading"
    value={heading}
    value-data-type={headingDataType}
    builder-context={builderContext}
    automatic-output-variables={automaticOutputVariables}
    api-version={apiVersion}
    onvaluechange={handleHeadingChange}
  ></c-flow-config-value-input>
</template>
```

### Inherited public API (do not redeclare)

`builderContext`, `inputVariables`, `genericTypeMappings`, `automaticOutputVariables`, `elementInfo`, `validate()`.

### Read

| Call                                   | Returns                                                        |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `this.input(name, fallback?, asRef?)`  | Saved value.                                                   |
| `this.reference(name, fallback?)`      | Saved value as `{!Resource}`.                                  |
| `this.inputVariable(name)`             | Raw variable including `valueDataType`.                        |
| `this.inputDataType(name, fallback?)`  | Saved `valueDataType`.                                         |
| `this.genericType(typeName, fallback?)`| Object API name bound to a generic mapping.                    |
| `this.apiVersion`                      | Flow runtime API version.                                      |

### Write

| Call                                             | Effect                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `this.setInput(name, value, dataType?)`          | Assign an input.                              |
| `this.clearInput(name, dataType?)`               | Remove an input assignment.                   |
| `this.setGenericType(typeName, typeValue)`       | Assign/clear a generic mapping.               |
| `this.applyCollectionChange({...})`              | Move collection + mapping + mirror + dependent together. Returns the transition. |

`applyCollectionChange` accepts `{ objectProperty, dependentProperty, typeName, newValue, objectType, currentObjectType, dependentValue, fallbackObjectType? }` and returns `{ changed, nextObjectType, clearDependent, showResetNotice }`.

### Validate

Override `validateConfiguration()` → `[{ key, errorString }]`. Also `setError(key, msg)`, `clearError(key)`, `clearErrors()`, `validationErrors`, `hasValidationErrors`.

Mark each control `data-validatable data-property="<name>"` so inherited `validate()` mirrors messages onto it.

### React to republished inputs

Override `configurationChanged(source)`; `source` is `builderContext` | `inputVariables` | `genericTypeMappings` | `automaticOutputVariables`. Flow Builder publishes them in **no guaranteed order** — never assume one has arrived when handling another.

---

## 5. Pickers

### `c-flow-config-value-input` — literal or resource scalar

`label`, `property-name`, `value`, `value-data-type`, `value-type` (`String`|`Number`), `builder-context`, `automatic-output-variables`, `api-version`, `required`, `placeholder`, `field-level-help`.

Event `valuechange` → `{ name, newValue, newValueDataType, resource }`.

Committed, restored, and manually pasted Flow references are validated against the expected scalar type. When metadata resolves an incompatible reference, `validationMessage` names the resource, its actual type/cardinality, and the required input shape; `reportValidity()` returns `false`. Unknown reference types remain allowed until Salesforce metadata resolves them.

Number literals must parse completely as finite numbers. Partially numeric or nonnumeric text is not committed and produces a contextual validation error.

### `c-flow-config-resource-picker` — Flow resource browser

Above, plus `accepted-types` (comma-separated; empty = all), `collection` (`any`|`only`|`exclude`), `allow-manual`, `allow-literal`, `allow-record-fields`, `literal-type`, `max-results`.

Event `resourcechange` → `{ name, newValue, newValueDataType, resource }`.

Committed, restored, and manually pasted references use the same `accepted-types` and `collection` rules as visible picker results. Known incompatibilities produce a contextual `validationMessage` and make `reportValidity()` return `false`; unresolved references remain allowed until metadata becomes available.

### `c-flow-config-field-picker` — SObject field selection

`label`, `property-name`, `object-api-name`, `value`, `multiple`, `sortable` (default `true`), `accepted-types`, `max-results`, `max-relationship-depth` (default 5), `required`, `placeholder`, `field-level-help`.

Event `fieldchange` → `{ name, newValue, newValueDataType, field, selectedValues, selectedFields }`.

Saved single and multiple fields are revalidated against `accepted-types` after field metadata resolves. Known incompatible paths report the selected field label/API path, actual Flow type, and required type. Unresolved legacy paths remain allowed.

### `c-flow-config-object-picker` — Salesforce object API-name selection

`label`, `property-name`, `value`, `available-object-types` (comma-separated or array; empty/`All` = no allowlist), `queryable-only`, `show-all` (default false), `max-results` (scroll-loaded batch size, default 200), `required`, `placeholder`, `field-level-help`.

Event `objectchange` → `{ name, newValue, newValueDataType, object, objectType }`. The selected API name is persisted as a Flow String. When `property-name` is supplied, selection and clearing also dispatch the standard Flow input-value event. The picker restores saved API names, groups standard and custom objects, and uses the shared picker popover and keyboard interaction. It initially shows user-facing standard, custom, and external objects. A root-level `Show all objects` switch reveals accessible feed/history/share/event/setting/internal objects and emits `filterchange` → `{ showAll }`. Reaching the bottom appends another `max-results` batch. Search and filter changes reset to the first batch. Missing-label markers fall back to API names.

### `c-flow-config-field-input` — field or custom value

Composes the field picker and scalar value input. Use it when a property normally selects a field from `object-api-name` but should optionally accept a custom literal or Flow resource. It accepts the field-picker attributes plus `value-data-type`, `builder-context`, `automatic-output-variables`, `api-version`, `allow-custom`, and controlled `custom-mode`.

When enabled, a `Custom value` switch appears in the shared picker header at the root level and immediately opens the alternate picker when toggled. The switch is hidden at nested browse levels and returns at the root. Persist `custom-mode` in an optional Boolean Flow property when the choice must survive closing and reopening the editor. Event `modechange` → `{ customMode }`; event `valuechange` → the active input detail plus `customMode`.

All picker inputs expose `setCustomValidity(message)`, `reportValidity()`, `validationMessage`.

---

## 6. Value formats — get these exactly right

| Kind                 | Stored as                              | `valueDataType` |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Flow resource        | `{!MyVariable}` / `{!varAccount.Name}` | `reference`     |
| Text literal         | `Some text`                            | `String`        |
| Number literal       | `42.5` (a number, not a string)        | `Number`        |
| Single field         | `Name` or `Account.Industry`           | `String`        |
| Multiple fields      | `["Name","Email"]` (JSON in a String)  | `String`        |
| Object API name      | `Account`                              | `String`        |

- References always keep the `{!...}` wrapper. Never strip it before saving.
- Clearing an input dispatches `configuration_editor_input_value_changed` with `newValue: null`. There is **no** `..._value_deleted` event; do not look for one.

---

## 7. Events on the wire

The framework dispatches these for you. Listed so you recognize them in tests.

```js
// assign or clear an input
new CustomEvent("configuration_editor_input_value_changed", {
  bubbles: true, composed: true, cancelable: false,
  detail: { name, newValue, newValueDataType }
});

// bind a generic SObject type
new CustomEvent("configuration_editor_generic_type_mapping_changed", {
  bubbles: true, composed: true, cancelable: false,
  detail: { typeName, typeValue }
});
```

`genericTypeMappings` entries use `{ typeName, typeValue }`. `inputVariables` entries use `{ name, value, valueDataType }`. These key names differ; mixing them up is the most common bug.

---

## 8. Recipes

### Scalar input

```js
static flowProperties = { heading: { type: "String" } };
```

### Record collection driving a field picker

```js
static flowProperties = {
  records: { type: "SObject", collection: true, genericType: "T",
             objectProperty: "objectApiName", required: true },
  displayField: { type: "field", dependsOn: "records", required: true }
};
```

Component meta needs `<propertyType name="T" extends="SObject" label="Record Type"/>`, `type="{T[]}"` for `records`, plus `String` properties for `objectApiName` and `displayField`.

### Ordered multi-field selection

```js
static flowProperties = {
  records: { type: "SObject", collection: true, genericType: "T" },
  columns: { type: "field", dependsOn: "records", multiple: true }
};
```

`columns` persists as a JSON array string. Parse with `JSON.parse` in the screen component.

### Two independent collections

Declare two resources with **different** `genericType` names and point each field at its own `dependsOn`:

```js
static flowProperties = {
  singleRecords: { type: "SObject", collection: true, genericType: "TSingle" },
  singleField: { type: "field", dependsOn: "singleRecords" },
  multipleRecords: { type: "SObject", collection: true, genericType: "TMultiple" },
  columns: { type: "field", dependsOn: "multipleRecords", multiple: true }
};
```

Component meta needs two `<propertyType>` declarations. Do not share one generic type between independent collections — it couples them, and clearing one will fight the other.

### Custom rule on top of a schema

```js
export default class MyEditor extends FlowConfigEditorBase {
  static flowProperties = { pageSize: { type: "Number" } };

  validateConfiguration() {
    const size = Number(this.input("pageSize"));
    return size > 0 && size <= 200
      ? []
      : [{ key: "pageSize", errorString: "Page Size must be between 1 and 200." }];
  }
}
```

---

## 9. Testing

`sfdx-lwc-jest`. Only `@api` members are reachable on the element host; internal helpers are not.

```js
import { createElement } from "lwc";
import MyEditor from "c/myComponentEditor";

const element = createElement("c-my-component-editor", { is: MyEditor });
element.builderContext = { variables: [
  { name: "accountList", dataType: "SObject", objectType: "Account", isCollection: true }
]};
element.inputVariables = [
  { name: "records", value: "accountList", valueDataType: "reference" }
];
document.body.appendChild(element);
await Promise.resolve();

expect(element.validate()).toEqual([]);
```

For a declarative editor, controls live inside the form's shadow root:

```js
element.shadowRoot
  .querySelector("c-flow-config-editor-form")
  .shadowRoot.querySelector('[data-property="records"]');
```

---

## 10. Install and deploy

```bash
sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org my-org
sf org assign permset --name Flow_Config_Editor_Access --target-org my-org
```

`Flow_Config_Editor_Access` grants the Apex controller and Visualforce bridge used for Apex-defined type and hierarchy-setting discovery. Apex source inspection additionally requires **Manage Flow**; without it the framework falls back to the Tooling API bridge, which enforces the user's own access.

---

## 11. Constraints an agent should respect

- Never hard-code an org's objects, fields, Apex classes, subflows, or screen components. Discovery must come from `builderContext` or Salesforce metadata.
- Treat `builderContext` as versioned external data. Tolerate missing arrays and alternate property names.
- Clone arrays out of `builderContext` before iterating; Flow Builder reuses them across republishes.
- Never log Flow values, session IDs, or metadata payloads.
- Do not redeclare inherited `@api` properties on an editor.
- Unsaved sibling screen-component outputs may not appear in `builderContext` yet. This is a platform limit, not a bug to work around.
- Keep `apiVersion` identical across `sfdx-project.json`, every `-meta.xml`, both manifests, and the Visualforce bridge. `npm run check:api-version` enforces it.

## 12. Verify your work

```bash
npm run verify
```

Runs API-version consistency, ESLint, Jest with coverage thresholds, and Prettier. All four must pass.
